title: Tech Note: Handling Pictures
featured_technology: READ PICTURE FILE / SAVE PICTURE TO FILE commands

historical_commentary.text: This note explains how 4D reads/writes picture files across native formats (PICT, BMP, GIF, JPEG, PSD, PSP) via QuickTime, and how to use PICTURE TO BLOB to convert between the original format and a working format so a picture's raw bytes can be manipulated directly. Since Apple's QuickTime framework (which underpinned 4D's picture format conversion at the time) has been fully discontinued, this note's specific QuickTime-dependent technique is obsolete, though 4D's newer, QuickTime-independent native picture format commands (introduced in later versions) address the same underlying need today.
related_updates: Apple discontinued QuickTime entirely (including QuickTime for Windows) around 2016, removing the technology this note's picture format conversion depended on

4D introduced native, QuickTime-independent picture format handling and conversion commands in later versions (following the 64-bit transition and QuickTime's removal from the OS), replacing this specific approach
PICTURE TO BLOB remains part of the current 4D language, but the underlying format-conversion engine it relies on is no longer QuickTime-based
